# Cost estimate

<!-- Generated by make cost (scripts/cost/estimate.mjs) from scripts/cost/prices.json and scripts/cost/usage.json. Do not edit: make docs-check fails when this file does not match those two files. -->

What the production architecture would cost a month if it were deployed to AWS in us-east-1 (US East, N. Virginia), at on-demand prices consulted on 2026-11-22.

> **An estimate, not a bill.** The prod stage was never deployed: it is synthesized and validated offline ([infrastructure.md](infrastructure.md)), and nothing here was ever charged to an AWS account. The volumes per invoice come from runs of the emulated cloud, the durations and the traffic are assumptions, and each one is declared [below](#assumptions). Taxes, support plans and the AWS account itself are not included.

How it is made: `scripts/cost/estimate.mjs`, a script without dependencies, computes every table on this page from two files: [`scripts/cost/prices.json`](../scripts/cost/prices.json) (each unit price with its official page, the AWS Price List API file it was read from, and the date) and [`scripts/cost/usage.json`](../scripts/cost/usage.json) (each assumption with its basis and its source). `make cost` writes this page again, and `make docs-check`, part of `make lint`, fails when the page does not match the two files.

## Summary

The fixed cost is what the month costs with no invoice at all, and the variable cost is the rest. Storage is priced for month 12 at a steady volume, so it holds 12 months of documents, database rows and logs. The free tier is left out, except in the last column. That column subtracts the always-free amounts, which the Price List itself prices at $0: Lambda, SQS, SNS, KMS, CloudWatch, CloudFront, EventBridge Scheduler, DynamoDB storage and 100 GB of data transfer out. It does not count a new account's credits or 12-month offers.

| Scenario | Invoices a month | Fixed | Variable | Total | Per 1,000 invoices | Total with the always-free tier |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Idle | 0 | $153.55 | $0.00 | **$153.55** | — | $145.54 |
| 10,000 invoices | 10,000 | $153.55 | $4.28 | **$157.83** | $15.78 | $148.21 |
| 100,000 invoices | 100,000 | $153.55 | $86.62 | **$240.16** | $2.40 | $220.58 |
| 1,000,000 invoices | 1,000,000 | $153.55 | $603.37 | **$756.92** | $0.76 | $709.40 |

With no invoice, the bill is the database's minimum capacity on two instances, the NAT gateway, the firewall, the keys, the secrets and observability: $153.55 a month, or $145.54 with the always-free tier.

## Levers

What each change to the prod stage would add (+) or save (−) a month, against the stage as it is, without the free tier.

| Lever | What changes | Idle | 10,000 invoices | 100,000 invoices | 1,000,000 invoices |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Remove the reader instance | The reader in the second zone goes away: a failover then waits for a new instance instead of promoting the reader ([infrastructure.md](infrastructure.md#when-something-fails)). | −$43.80 | −$43.80 | −$65.70 | −$131.40 |
| Turn on RDS Proxy | RDS Proxy in front of the database, billed per ACU of the database instances, with a minimum of 8 ACUs. | +$87.60 | +$87.60 | +$87.60 | +$87.60 |
| Turn on the interface endpoints | The 5 AWS services without a gateway endpoint get an interface endpoint in each of the 2 zones; their traffic leaves the NAT gateway. | +$73.00 | +$72.97 | +$72.67 | +$69.71 |
| Add a second NAT gateway | One NAT gateway, with its address, in each zone, so losing one zone still leaves a way out. | +$36.50 | +$36.50 | +$36.50 | +$36.50 |
| CloudFront PriceClass_100 | Edge locations in North America, Europe and Israel only: viewers in Colombia are served from North America, at its prices and with more latency. | $0.00 | −$0.09 | −$0.92 | −$9.20 |
| Keep logs 30 days | Every log group keeps its logs 30 days instead of 365, so storage holds one month of logs instead of 12. | −$0.08 | −$0.17 | −$1.01 | −$9.35 |
| Remove the metrics and alarms | No custom metric, alarm, composite alarm or dashboard; the logs stay, and nothing pages anyone. | −$12.60 | −$12.60 | −$12.60 | −$12.60 |
| Move the functions to arm64 | Every function on Graviton, priced 20 % lower per GB-second; the functions' image must be built for arm64. | −$0.05 | −$0.25 | −$2.07 | −$20.30 |

## Assumptions

Every value the estimate uses, from [`scripts/cost/usage.json`](../scripts/cost/usage.json), per invoice unless its unit says otherwise. The measurements were taken on 2026-11-23. The emulator (Floci) runs the local stage on one machine, so its timings are not AWS's: the durations below are assumptions, and the emulator's figures are only their floor.

Each database instance's average capacity is an assumption too, since no load test has measured it: 0.5 ACU idle, 0.5 ACU at 10,000 invoices, 0.75 ACU at 100,000 invoices, 1.5 ACU at 1,000,000 invoices.

## Not in the estimate

- Taxes, a support plan, and the costs of the AWS account, its organization and its security services (CloudTrail beyond the free trail, GuardDuty, Security Hub).
- The domain and its DNS: no hosted zone is managed here ([deployment.md](deployment.md)). The ACM certificate is free.
- Data transfer between the two zones, within the region: the functions run in both and the database writer in one.
- Retries, failures and drills: the scenarios count each invoice's happy path, as make cloud-check measures it.
- The deployments: continuous integration, the image builds and the web app uploads.
- Savings Plans, reserved capacity, and a new account's 12-month offers and credits.
